Q: Convert relative time (in hours before or after a point in time) to clock time A:

You can use as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()) to retrieve the default 00:00:00 local time, and then apply the offset (Hours * 60 minutes * 60 seconds)

format(as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()) + hours*3600, "%H:%M")

and you will see

[1] "22:00" "22:30" "00:00" "02:30" "04:00"

If you don't mind dates and also keep the Date format, you can simply run

as.POSIXct(Sys.Date()) + hours*3600

which gives

[1] "2026-03-10 22:00:00 UTC" "2026-03-10 22:30:00 UTC"
[3] "2026-03-11 00:00:00 UTC" "2026-03-11 02:30:00 UTC"
[5] "2026-03-11 04:00:00 UTC"

Q: What is an Interface in Java? A:

I think that List is a great example of a use of an interface. It tells you that you can do things like get, clear, set, add etc. That means that if I hand you a List, you can do all of those things to it.

But it doesn't tell you anything about how that List is implemented: it could be an ArrayList (it's backed by an array), it could be a LinkedList (it's backed by objects that point to each other), it could be something completely different. ArrayList and LinkedList are fundamentally different to one another, but because they implement all of those methods, they are functionally interchangable - so you don't need to care about how the List is implemented.

Q: Best way to 'Update if exists, or Insert' A:

Every one of them has different purpose, pros and cons.

Option 1 is good for multi row inserts/updates. However It only checks primary key constraints. It does not work on SQL Server, it does work on other RDBMS.

Option 2 is good for small sets of data. Single record insertion/update. It is more like script.

Option 3 is best for big queries. Lets say, reading from one table and inserting/updating to another accordingly. You can define which condition to be satisfied for insertion and/or update. You are not limited to primary key/unique constraint.
